title: Ravya bar Kisi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Yoma 42b, Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta and the Rabbis disagree about the weight of the strip of the red heifer, and Rabbi Yirmeyah of Difti said to Ravina: “They do not disagree about the heifer but about the scapegoat.” “And that day Ravya bar Kisi died, and they gave a mnemonic for it: Ravya bar Kisi atones like the scapegoat.” Rashi explains: on the day they disagreed about it, Ravya bar Kisi died. Hyman reads Rashi as referring to Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta’s time; Hyman’s own plain-sense reading is that Ravya bar Kisi died in Ravina’s time. This is also Yuchasin’s view, which reads: “Ravina said: Rabbi Yirmeyah of Difta told me (in the Gemara it reads ‘Rabbi Yirmeyah of Difti said to Ravina,’ but in Dikdukei Soferim the reading is as in Yuchasin, and Hyman considers this to remove the objection in the work Maskil LeEitan): the reason is the scapegoat; and they gave the mnemonic ‘Ravya bar Kisi atones,’ for he died then.”
In Chullin 20b we find Ravin bar Kisi, and in Bava Batra 63a Ravina bar Kisi.

notes.text: Ravya bar Kisi is the one who died in the proposed Ravina-era reading, not Ravina dying in his own days. Maskil LeEitan is the full work title. Hyman’s Rashi interpretation and Yuchasin/Dikdukei Soferim alternatives remain attributed.

The consulted dispute and death mnemonic are at Yoma 42a, while Hyman supplies 42b. The Gemara names Ravya [bar] Kisi. Rashi’s inspected gloss says he died on the disputed day and calls it a sage’s name; it does not explicitly resolve Hyman’s competing era interpretations. Exact Yuchasin and Dikdukei Soferim editions remain uninspected.
